items.content:
Karoline has been a great friend and an incredible partner in advancing President Trump’s America First agenda.

She is a fighter who has never backed down from defending the President, this administration, and the millions of Americans who support Making America Great Again. I have always valued her judgment, her candor, and her unwavering commitment to our country and the American people.

I have tremendous respect for her decision to put family first, and I am grateful for her friendship and all she has done for this administration.

Karoline has a very bright future ahead, and I know she will remain a powerful voice for President Trump and the America First movement. It has been an honor serving alongside you.Karoline Leavitt (@karolineleavitt)Serving as the White House Press Secretary over the past year and a half has been the honor and adventure of a lifetime. I am incredibly grateful to President Trump for granting me so many extraordinary opportunities, such as working in the West Wing and spending countless hours in the Oval Office, flying around the world and meeting foreign leaders, and traveling across our beautiful country and meeting Americans from all walks of life.

Most of all, I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium. I have spoken with great pride about the many historic accomplishments of this Administration, and I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump’s successes. 

Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least. The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life.

President Trump has asked me to continue serving as a top advisor to him on the outside, and I will always remain a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party. 

Our country is facing an existential threat from an increasingly extremist Democrat Party that seeks to destroy everything great about America, and I believe it is incumbent upon all of us who care about this country to fight back against that threat. My fight is entering a new phase, but it is far from over.

Thank you again to the President, the First Lady, and the entire Trump family for your kindness and generosity over the years. Thank you to our amazing Chief of Staff Susie Wiles for empowering me since the day she hired me on the campaign, and to the President’s cabinet, my staff, colleagues, and friends at the White House who work so hard on behalf of our nation. It has been a privilege to serve alongside so many accomplished and impressive people, and I look forward to cheering them on over the next two and a half years. 

And of course, thank you most especially to my loving and supportive husband and family for the sacrifices they made for me to serve in this role. ♥️🇺🇸—  https://x.com/karolineleavitt/status/2087625708554100999 
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 12, 2026

items.title: Today’s action is a victory for common sense and American small businesses. @POTUS promised to cut red tape, and this final rule delivers. Treasury is eliminating a burdensome reporting requirement for millions of law-abiding business owners without compromising our national security.
items.content:
Today’s action is a victory for common sense and American small businesses.  @POTUS promised to cut red tape, and this final rule delivers. Treasury is eliminating a burdensome reporting requirement for millions of law-abiding business owners without compromising our national security.Treasury Department (@USTreasury)Today,  @FinCENnews issued a final rule that permanently removes the requirement for U.S. companies and U.S. persons to report beneficial ownership information. FinCEN today also announced that it will delete previously reported information by U.S. persons from the beneficial ownership information database.—  https://x.com/USTreasury/status/2087269903334265280 
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 11, 2026

items.content:
It was an honor to join  @SecWar , Senator Darline Graham, and Governor  @henrymcmaster in renaming Joint Base Charleston in memory of Lindsey Graham.

The names we place on our military installations reflect the service we honor, the character we esteem, and the example we ask future generations to follow. Few Americans embodied those virtues more completely than Lindsey.

He served our nation for 33 years in uniform and more than three decades in the United States Senate, always guided by his belief that the first obligation of government is to keep the American people safe.

Across both of his callings in life, whether the pull of duty brought him to the Air Force or to Congress, a base in Afghanistan or the floor of the Senate, he devoted himself to the same great purpose. He served a cause greater than self.

That is why this base will bear Lindsey's name with pride. And the soldiers who serve beneath it will find in his legacy an example to guide their own.

His name will forever stand as a testament to a life devoted to service, sacrifice, and country. 
Video

— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 10, 2026

items.content:
With President Trump’s policies, the fundamentals for American prosperity are in place because American workers are the best in the world. Today’s jobs report understates the underlying strength of the real economy: Main Street is building, factories are producing, and workers are becoming more productive. July marks the 5th straight month of goods-producing job growth. By creating 105K jobs so far this year, goods-producing employment has had the best 7-month start since 2023. Additionally, productivity growth rose more than double the rate expected in Q2, bolstering the conditions for durable growth and real wage gains for American workers.

Strong Q3 growth expectations further show that the economy is positioned to accelerate. When America produces more and workers become more productive, Main Street wins: higher wages, stronger businesses, more options for customers, and a durable expansion built on inflation-reducing supply-side strength rather than a temporary sugar high.
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) Aug 7, 2026
